text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: elevated 5xx rates from customer QuellOps on Dedicated-cluster-17. Auto-alert: gateway errors + timeouts. See metric spike: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1962500000 :rotating_light:

oncall-nate: I'm on it. Acknowledge. Any immediate customer impact figures?

sre-amber: Looking now — cluster-17 shows 5xx rate from 0.2% -> 8.7% in the last 6m. Latency p95 up from 120ms -> 820ms. Errors concentrated on nodes gpu-node-17-[2..4].

eng-runtime-max: tagging in. Hypothesis: noisy-tenant eviction or GPU memory pressure. I'll check kernel OOMs / nvml.

sre-amber: Also see elevated queue length on runtime-proxy and repeated 502s from the model servers.

support-liz: Customer QuellOps Slack in parallel: "we're seeing 5xx on all POST /generate calls". They've opened a ticket RED-3129.

eng-runtime-max: Running quick checks: 
```
# check GPU mem
ssh node@gpu-node-17-2 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv'
# check processes
ssh node@gpu-node-17-2 'ps -eo pid,cmd,etimes | grep runtime_server'
```

eng-runtime-max: nvml shows memory at ~98% on node-17-2, and the runtime process has grown over expected KV cache size. Looks like large prefix caching from tenant "quell-ml"? need to confirm.

oncall-nate: If it's tenant-level noisy neighbor, let's apply eviction policy per runbook. Amber, can you run eviction script on node-17-2 first and drain if needed?

sre-amber: Running eviction (runbook: Dedicated -> noisy-neighbor -> eviction). Command:
```
/runbooks/dedicated/noisy-evict.sh --node gpu-node-17-2 --tenant quell-ml --grace 30s
```

sre-amber: Eviction submitted. Also flipping routing to fallback pool for QuellOps to avoid total customer outage: `route set --customer=quellops --pool=fallback-small-v2 --duration=15m`

product-maya: Noted. Please coordinate with support so QuellOps sees minimal disruption and we provide a timeline.

support-liz: Telling customer: "We've detected a noisy workload in your cluster. We're initiating a short failover and eviction; you should see reduced errors in ~5-10min. We'll follow up with RCA."

eng-runtime-max: Evict script log: 
```
[00:12:24] evict: tenant=quell-ml -> cordon
[00:12:38] migrate_kv: flushing 9.2GB prefix cache
[00:12:55] evict: succeeded, processes terminated gracefully
```

eng-runtime-max: After eviction, immediate memory freed on node-17-2. Metrics trending back down. p95 now 260ms, 5xx rate 1.1% and falling.

sre-amber: Confirming across cluster-17: node-17-3 shows similar pressure though not as severe — might be cross-tenant accumulation. I'll run `cache-prune` on affected nodes as a precaution.

oncall-nate: Good. Are there any API gateway logs showing retries that could have amplified load?

eng-runtime-max: Gateway logs show client retries (3xx retry loops) from the QuellOps SDK due to timeouts; they were set to aggressive backoff=1s x3. Recommend support ask QuellOps to reduce client retries for now; we've enabled a short ingress rate-limit for them to avoid thrashing: `ingress-limit set --customer=quellops --rps=50 --duration=30m`.

support-liz: Sent message to customer ops: "We've applied a temporary request rate cap and routed you to a fallback pool. Please avoid manual retries for the next 20m while we stabilize." They responded: "Thanks, seeing huge improvement already."

product-maya: Quick customer impact summary for the exec ping: QuellOps experienced ~8.7% 5xx at peak, affecting ~12% of their requests in the 6m window. No data loss; some requests retried. We applied eviction, cache flush, ingress cap, and fallback routing. Recovery visible within 10m of mitigation.

eng-runtime-max: Noted one anomaly in logs during eviction: a few model server instances failed to restart due to unavailable GPU resources; autoscaler was at max for that shard. I've kicked a manual scale-up on dedicated pool: `dedicated-scale --pool cluster-17 --add-nodes 2 --reason "post-eviction buffer"`.

sre-amber: Scale up accepted by autoscaler; new nodes provisioning. Will keep monitoring. Also scheduled an alert suppression for noisy-neighbor policy for 20m to avoid alert storms.

incident-bot: Incident update: RED-3129 created, severity P2, impacted customer: QuellOps, mitigation actions: eviction, fallback routing, ingress limit, cache prune, scale-up. Link: https://incidents.redwood/RED-3129

oncall-nate: Handoff: I'm going offline in ~25m. Handoff to @sre-amber. Amber, please keep the incident in watch for another 2 hours and coordinate with support for extended customer comms + postmortem.

sre-amber: Will take it. Current status: recovery progressing, 5xx < 0.5%, p95 140ms, nodes stable. Next steps: 1) verify tenant-specific cache settings, 2) review autoscaler thresholds, 3) schedule follow-up with QuellOps to tune client retries and prefix caching.

support-liz: I'll schedule a customer call and include a short timeline + mitigation steps.

customer-quellops: Thanks team — saw errors drop within ~8m after your actions. We'll await RCA and will adjust client retry behavior. Appreciate the quick handling. :thumbsup:

product-maya: Logging action items to RED-3129: assign eng-runtime for root-cause and a follow-up to consider per-tenant cache caps and early throttling.

eng-runtime-max: Quick note for RCA: likely combination of large prefix caching (customer-side workload) + aggressive client retries causing sustained GPU memory pressure. We'll draft remediation: per-tenant cache quotas, early request shedding, and better autoscale headroom.

sre-amber: Closing timeboxed mitigation: will keep monitoring until last_message_ts. If metrics stay stable for 1h, we'll mark mitigated in the incident system.

oncall-nate: Thanks all. Leaving channel.

incident-bot: This thread was updated with post-mitigation metrics snapshot and assigned to eng-runtime for RCA.
